precepts.text: How long shall it be to the end of these wonders? A time, times, and an half: a time is a hundred years, times is two hundred, and an half: 350 years, and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people. Within those 350 years we were totally destroyed: we forgot who we are, we even forgot our nationality. After 70 AD our country was destroyed, but we still built cities in Africa, still had kings and governments, still knew we were the children of Israel. It was within the slave trade and colonization that the power was scattered.
precepts.point: Without the ephod: no priest there to guide you and tell you what God needs you to do. That's the religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance stripped away.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
Hosea says the children of Israel “shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod”. Daniel 12 gives the time frame for it. “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?” The wonders are our people being destroyed, enslaved and colonized, being without a king, without a prince, without an ephod.

“it shall be for a time, times, and an half”. A time is a hundred years; times is two hundred, three hundred in all; and an half makes 350 years. “and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.” Within those 350 years we were totally destroyed. All that power was gone from us; we forgot who we are, and we even forgot our nationality.

When we fled Jerusalem in 70 AD, was our power destroyed? Our country was destroyed, but we went to Africa and built cities there, and the ten tribes were set up on this side of the world doing their thing too. We still had governments, we still had kings over us, and we still knew we were the children of Israel. It was within the slave trade and colonization that the power of the holy people was scattered.

That is the many days without a king: without political sovereignty, when Europe colonized Ghana, Nigeria, Angola, Senegal, Papua New Guinea and the Congo, and when the transatlantic slave trade took us. It is without an image: our minds destroyed until the sisters in Africa bleach their skin and put on weaves, because worshipping the God of your oppressor destroys the way you look at yourself. The same curses fell on our people all over Africa, like the Mau Mau in Kenya, tortured in British camps and paid less than 4,000 pounds each. That is why I don't want no damn reparations.

precepts.text: From the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up.
precepts.point: Without the ephod: no priest there to guide you and tell you what God needs you to do. That's the religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance stripped away.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
Daniel 12 gives the time frame for when our people would be without a king, without an image, and without a sacrifice, as Hosea 3:4 says. Verse 11 reads: “And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.”

The daily sacrifice taken away is Hosea's “without a sacrifice”. Without the sacrifice, the image and the ephod, all our religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance was stripped away, and there was no priest to guide us and tell us what God needs us to do. The white man came in, whipped us, taught us white Jesus and his lies, and forced it down our throats in Africa. After he brought the slaves over here, he went to Africa and destroyed them there, until the people in Africa don't even know that we in the Caribbean and America are the same people.

So from the taking away of the sacrifice, the days are counted, and the question Daniel asked, “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?”, is answered with a set time. That goes back to the yoke of iron upon thy neck until thou have been destroyed: it did not just happen to us over here, it happened to our people in Africa, and the scattering of the holy people runs its appointed course.

precepts.text: Many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. When you die you go to sleep, yes; but Christ has the power to wake you up: some to everlasting life, and some to shame.
precepts.point: The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us. What was just went over is a secret thing that Moses understood: he understood we would be brought into spiritual Egypt, into America, and he saw America destroyed.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
Christ has the power over life and death, which is why Daniel 12 says some shall awake. “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

Many of them are going to awake. Some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. When you die, you go to sleep, yes. But Christ has the power to wake your behind up and torment you.

That is what stands behind the carcases of Isaiah 66:24, whose worm does not die and whose fire is not quenched, and behind the land of Deuteronomy 29 that is all brimstone, salt and burning. Those who forsook the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers and served other gods do not simply die and disappear: they are awakened to shame and everlasting contempt. As 2 Esdras 9 says, read in the same moment, those who despised his law while the place of repentance was open “must know it after death by pain.” And the righteous awake to everlasting life, the seed and the name that remain.

precepts.text: The secret place of the Most High is the Bible; the arrow that flieth by day is the missile and the destruction that wasteth at noonday; a thousand shall fall at thy side and ten thousand at thy right hand but it shall not come nigh thee, and his angels bear thee up: the deliverance of the Israelites in the midst of Armageddon, which Satan twisted to tell Christ to jump.
precepts.point: Many that sleep in the dust shall awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame. They that be wise, who study, pray and apply, shine as the firmament. The book was sealed to the time of the end, so the open understanding coming out now shows we are in it, and knowledge has increased.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Daniel says “there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered”. What makes this tribulation different is World War III and Armageddon, and Psalm 91 shows how Israel is delivered in the midst of it.

“He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” The secret place of the Most High is the Bible.

“Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day; Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” The arrow that flieth by day is the missile, the destruction that wasteth at noonday.

“A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.” And “he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.”

That is the deliverance of the Israelites in the midst of Armageddon: thy people delivered, every one found written in the book, not all nations. It is the same psalm Satan twisted when he told Christ to jump from the pinnacle of the temple.

precepts.text: Great fearfulness and trembling, storms from the south, north, west and east, the four winds, and a horrible star and flying swords, the ICBM and the missiles, that break down cities and walls and go steadfastly unto Babylon, America, and make her afraid, and they that be about her bewail her as Revelation 18 says.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Daniel's “time of trouble, such as never was” is World War III and Armageddon. Ezra shows it: “And there shall be great fearfulness and trembling upon earth: and they that see the wrath shall be afraid, and trembling shall come upon them.”

“And then shall there come great storms from the south, and from the north, and another part from the west. And strong winds shall arise from the east”: storms from all four winds.

They “shall pour out over every high and eminent place an horrible star, Fire, and hail, and flying swords”. The horrible star is the ICBM, and the flying swords are the missiles. “And they shall break down the cities and walls, mountains and hills, trees of the wood, and grass of the meadows, and their corn.”

“And they shall go stedfastly unto Babylon, and make her afraid.” Babylon is America. And “then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her”, just as Revelation 18 says the kings and merchants of the earth will bewail her. That is the time of trouble in which Daniel's people, every one written in the book, shall be delivered.

precepts.text: Satan used Psalm 91 to say cast thyself down; Christ answered thou shalt not tempt the Lord, because the psalm is about the deliverance of Israel, not a dare.
precepts.point: Many that sleep in the dust shall awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame. They that be wise, who study, pray and apply, shine as the firmament. The book was sealed to the time of the end, so the open understanding coming out now shows we are in it, and knowledge has increased.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Psalm 91 promises the deliverance of Israel in the time of trouble: “He shall give his angels charge over thee”. Satan used that same psalm on Christ: “And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence”.

“For it is written, He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee: And in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.” Satan twisted the psalm into a dare, telling Christ to jump.

“And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.” Christ answered that way because the psalm is not a dare to test God. It is about the deliverance of Israel in the midst of Armageddon, when a thousand fall at our side and ten thousand at our right hand, and the angels bear us up.

precepts.text: After three days and a half the spirit of life entered them and they stood on their feet, which is now, and great fear fell on them which saw them; then come up hither. Between standing up and deliverance John left out tribulation, World War III and Armageddon, which the precepts supply; the Israelites who want to invest in airplanes and boats do not believe the angels are coming.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Daniel says “at that time thy people shall be delivered”. John shows the order of it: “And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” That standing up is now.

“And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them.” Between the standing up and the deliverance, John left out the tribulation, World War III and Armageddon; the precepts supply it. Tribulation has to come, then World War III, then Armageddon, when Christ comes in the midst of World War III.

“And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand: and the remnant were affrighted, and gave glory to the God of heaven.” A great destruction.

The Israelites who want to invest in airplanes and boats to get out do not believe the angels are coming. Come up hither is the deliverance: the angels bear us up, as Psalm 91 says.

precepts.text: Many that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
precepts.point: Because thou hast kept the word of my patience I will keep thee from the hour of temptation which shall come upon all the world: Jacob's trouble leading into World War III and Armageddon. No force field; they are at rest. The righteous perisheth and no man layeth it to heart, but merciful men are taken away from the evil to come; they enter into peace and rest in their beds, each walking in his uprightness, and many that sleep in the dust shall awake. That is why when brothers and sisters die I do not do the tears.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Isaiah 57 says the righteous “shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness”: they are not dead. Daniel 12 says the same thing.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake”. Those that sleep in the dust are the ones that died, and they shall awake, “some to everlasting life”: the righteous brothers and the righteous sisters; “and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

“And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.”

So the saints who died keeping the word of Christ’s patience are only sleeping. They were kept from the hour of temptation that comes upon all the world, Jacob’s trouble, and they will awake to everlasting life. That is why we do not grieve the righteous the way the world does.

precepts.text: Michael shall stand up for the children of thy people, and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book. Israel is written in the book of life, not everybody. Jeremiah 46:28: fear thou not, O Jacob, for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee, but I will not make a full end of thee; I will correct thee in measure, yet not leave thee wholly unpunished. 2 Esdras 9:22: let the multitude perish which was born in vain, and let my grape be kept, for with great labour have I made it perfect.
precepts.point: For, behold, the Lord cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity; the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain. Jeremiah 51:49: as Babylon hath caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth. Revelation 18:24: in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth. The judgment on this kingdom will be the worst of all.

note.label: War & the Pain of Repentance

precepts.why:
Revelation 20 says whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire. So who is written in the book of life? Is it the Chinese, the white man, or the Arabs? Daniel answers.

“And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time.” That is the indignation of Isaiah 26, when God's people must “enter thou into thy chambers” and hide “until the indignation be overpast.” There will be so much devastation that we will be fearful.

“And at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.” Who is written in the book of life? Israel, Daniel's people. Not everybody.

Jeremiah says the same, and they hate this one: “Fear thou not, O Jacob my servant, saith the Lord: for I am with thee; for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure; yet will I not leave thee wholly unpunished.” God is correcting us in measure, but he will not destroy us.

And Ezra: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain; and let my grape be kept, and my plant; for with great labour have I made it perfect.” All the nations were born in vain; the Israelites are the grape and the plant that is kept. So when the Lord comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth, Israel written in the book is delivered, and all the nations go into the lake of fire.

precepts.text: Many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
precepts.point: All that are in the graves shall hear his voice, and shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.” Daniel saw the same two resurrections: “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

Some to everlasting life, some to shame and everlasting contempt: the resurrection of life and the resurrection of damnation. “The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live.” That happened before their eyes with Lazarus, and it reaches forward to the last judgment, when all that are in the graves hear his voice and awake, as Daniel wrote.

precepts.text: Daniel is told he shall stand in his lot at the end of days; every prophet comes back and stands in his lot, picking up the same Bible and teaching again.
precepts.point: They insist Christ broke the Sabbath even though Peter and Paul testified that Christ did no sin, which shows the same spirit that was on the Pharisees is on the Christian pastors. The work the Sabbath forbids is occupational labor, not healing or picking corn to eat, and their real motive was envy, because the disciples gathered and unified the people and their control and money were being touched.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Daniel was told, “go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.” Every prophet comes back and stands in his lot, picking up the same Bible and teaching again.

That is why the spirit that was on the Pharisees is being activated again. Everyone plays their role again in this lifetime. Just as the disciples are back in the truth, the chief priests, Sadducees and Pharisees are back too, laying hands on the men who teach and saying the same things they said before.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth”: those that have died, “shall awake”: you shall awake from your chambers. “Some to everlasting life”: that’s what you want. Those who have died shall awake to everlasting life.

Now the next part: “and some to shame and everlasting contempt.” Everlasting. There’s no reprieve, there’s no oh, now I’m good. Once that is done, it’s done. Another word for contempt is torment: damnation, same thing. That is the not being forgiven in the world to come.

note.label: Who & What is the Abomination of Desolation

precepts.why: The precept with that: “from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days”, which is about three years and seven months. We’re still talking about the abomination of desolation, the same thing we read in 1 Maccabees 1, and the cleansing we read in 1 Maccabees 4, verses 41 to 56.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

precepts.why:
“And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people”: he stands for the children of God’s people, the Israelites. “And there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.” If your name is written in the book, brothers, that means you fulfilled your purpose. That’s why your name is in the book: you fulfilled what was predestinated for you.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life”: those that rise up to everlasting life fulfilled their purpose while they lived. “And some to shame and everlasting contempt”: those that wake up to shame and everlasting contempt did not fulfill their purpose. Their purpose was to keep the commandments; that’s the whole duty of man, and they didn’t fulfill it.

“And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.” So you brothers out here teaching the gospel, the Bible says you going to shine as the stars for ever and ever. You going to be illuminated; that’s why he says gold, a golden wedge. You going to shine for real, the illumination going to come from you. But you got to remember: you got to fulfill your purpose.

note.label: The Evolution Of Revolutionaries

precepts.why:
“How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?” The wonders are us being scattered in slavery and destroyed.

The man clothed in linen swore “that it shall be for a time, times, and an half”. A time is 100 years, times 200 more, and the half 50: we would be enslaved and worn out by this man for 350 years. The same count as the time and times and the dividing of time in Daniel 7:25.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 20

precepts.why: Meditate on scriptures like this before you do some evil. “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life”: that is the first resurrection. “And some to shame and everlasting contempt”: that is damnation.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 20

precepts.why: Who is in the book of life: “And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people.” “And at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.”

note.label: Living Martyrs

precepts.why:
Christ says it: he that heareth my word and believeth on him that sent me “shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.” Then: “Marvel not at this”: don’t be shocked at what I just said, “for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice.” The graves are the chambers of death where all souls rest.

“And shall come forth; they that have done good”: those that kept the commandments in the faith of Christ, “unto the resurrection of life.” That is the everlasting life of Daniel 12. “And they that have done evil”: you break the commandments, you don’t have faith in Christ, “unto the resurrection of damnation.” That is the shame and everlasting contempt of Daniel 12:2. The wicked do not die and come back righteous. They come back to damnation.

note.label: Living Martyrs

precepts.why:
“And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith, whereby ye have believed.” In order for us to be saved we must have works, that is the commandments, and faith, that is in Christ. Be mindful of the brothers and sisters who have been in this body three, four, five, eight years and have no works, who do nothing and want to be part of nothing. Those are idle spirits. If they do nothing here, they do nothing at home, and if you marry one, watch all kind of hell break loose in the house.

Those with works and faith “Shall be preserved from the said perils”, the said dangers, “and shall see my salvation in my land, and within my borders”, because we are going to be in the wilderness, “for I have sanctified them for me from the beginning”: before the creation of the world.

“Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways.” Some men and women have the opportunity, but they abuse God’s ways: I got grace in Christ, I got grace in Yahawashi, so to hell with those laws. The Lord sees you, and you better fear the Lord. “And they that have cast them away despitefully”, cast away God’s laws, “shall dwell in torments.” That is Daniel 12:2. That is John 5:24 and 29, saying the same thing. There are groups that say there is no torment when Christ returns. Oh, there is going to be torment.

“For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me”: like the church system that gets financial benefits and all kinds of benefits, and says you don’t have to keep his laws, they are done away with. “And they that have loathed my law”: that is the key. There are Israelite camps right now that hate the law; when we talk about the law they say F that law stuff. You know who you are, and the Lord does too. “While they had yet liberty”, as you have liberty right now, “and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it.” The place of repentance is open to you now, and all we can do is warn the men and women in those foolish congregations.

“The same must know it after death by pain.” Not right now, because right now when you die you are at rest. But when Christ returns with the keys of hell and of death, he is going to raise some up to everlasting life and some to everlasting condemnation.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
Shine forth as the morning: “And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament.” Those of us that are wise, in the kingdom, shall shine as the brightness of the firmament, the same way Moses did, who had to wear a veil. That will happen to all Israel.

“And they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.” We are going to shine forever and ever, as the noonday itself.

note.label: What's The 1000 Year Reign?

precepts.why: How do you know the book in the right hand of him that sat on the throne in Revelation 5 is the Bible? This is how we know. “But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end”: meaning the Bible would be sealed until the end times. What time are we living in now? The end times. “Many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased”: the white man’s knowledge shall be increased. So now we know that that book is the Bible.

note.label: Gods Memorial: The Smoke of Her Torment

precepts.why:
You all think you escape: you get blown up by the nuclear bombs, you just go to sleep and that’s it. Nah, that’s just the beginning of it for all you adulterers, murderers, haters, brothers that don’t want to repent, sisters that don’t want to repent. “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth”: when you’re dead you go to sleep. When Christ returns, if you’re wicked and dead you ain’t sleeping, and if you’re righteous you ain’t sleeping neither.

They “shall awake, some to everlasting life”: when they arise they wake up to everlasting life, meaning they are going to live forever. “And some to shame and everlasting contempt”: that goes back to the time of the dead, that they should be judged. Some will be awakened to shame and everlasting contempt, meaning your behind is about to be tormented, about to be cast in the Lake of Fire.

Remember what happened with Samuel, when the witch woke Samuel up. Samuel said, why have you disquieted me, why you wake me up? She woke him up in the spirit realm, and he was talking through her. That shows things in the spirit realm that we don’t fully understand.

Read with Revelation 11:18 again: the reward to the servants, the prophets, is everlasting life, and some are going to awake to shame and everlasting contempt. It is not talking about a physical realm for the wicked when it says they shall awake.

note.label: The 4 Temples In Jerusalem

precepts.why: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people”, “and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.” The only ones written in the book are Daniel’s people: the Israelites. Not Moab and Ammon and all the other nations.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
Here is the war such as never was. “And this shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet”: that’s only done by a nuclear missile. “And their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth. And it shall come to pass in that day, that a great tumult from the Lord shall be among them”.

That right there is what’s going to happen in this third world war when Christ returns. That’s what it means, a time of trouble such as never was.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
The precept to Zechariah 14:12. It talks about missiles in the Bible; the Bible talks about everything. “Behold, I have created the smith”: the smith there is Oppenheimer. “The smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.” That’s what Oppenheimer said when he created the atom bomb: now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds.

Then we read in 2 Esdras 11 where it said ‘the end of this your time’ shall come through them. These are the people that are going to bring about the end of this civilization that we see today.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: Our spirits don’t stay in the ground. “Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth?” So when we go back to Daniel 12:2, “many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake”, we know our spirits are not in the earth. We go up before the Lord.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: Remember when Samuel died, and King Saul said to the witch, summon Samuel, tell me what you see? That’s why I need y’all to study, pray, apply. “And the king said unto her, Be not afraid: for what sawest thou? And the woman said unto Saul, I saw gods ascending out of the earth.” Ascending, ascending, ascending out of the earth. Who knows the spirit of man that goeth upward: that’s what we just read in Ecclesiastes.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

That everlasting contempt. “And at that time thy people shall be delivered”: Daniel’s people are gonna be delivered from that destruction that’s gonna be taking place here. When Europe drops them bombs on America, we’re gonna be delivered through that.

What’s so crazy is you always see a dumb Christian talking about, I’m saved; brother, are you saved, sister, are you saved; come let me dip you in some water. They dip people in a pool where people pee in that pool water and say, you are clean, you are saved. And every last brother and sister that left IUIC being evil, all of them went and got baptized. How is dipping yourself in water gonna save you from them nuclear bombs that’s about to hit this place? Ducking yourself in a pool ain’t gonna save you from thermonuclear destruction.
